overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance data clearly highlights 'What If / Extreme Space Scenario' videos as the dominant growth driver for FACTVERSE. Videos utilizing speculative planetary scenarios (e.g., 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?', 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?') generated significantly higher views-per-day and stronger engagement (likes-per-view) compared to standard trivia facts or psychology micro-topics published in the same timeframe. Standard exotic space facts (like supersonic rubies or coal-dark planets) also outperform standard animal or brain facts, indicating that astronomical anomalies and hypothetical physics scenarios hold the highest retention and curiosity value for our audience.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1024 views in ~4 days) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (970 views in ~8 days) massively outperform standard declarative statements.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If' speculative physics and space disaster scenarios. Structure the narrative around immediate sensory immersion followed by a shocking scientific reality.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles detailing bizarre weather or planetary compositions (e.g., 'The Planet Darker Than Coal', 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') consistently secure high velocity within their first 7 days.
winning_patterns.action: Continue sourcing lesser-known exoplanets with extreme physical properties (extreme pressure, weird light absorption, impossible rain) for future space shorts.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' or 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' lingered at low view counts (5-71 views) with minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychology and cognitive fact shorts unless paired with a high-stakes, bizarre historical mystery or extreme survival angle.

weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts (e.g., 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts', 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever') underperformed relative to our space content, showing lower engagement rates.
weak_patterns.action: Shift animal content away from simple trivia toward cinematic animal survival or prehistoric crossovers (e.g., deep-sea abyssal horrors).

next_video.reason: Leverages the proven high-performing 'What If' structural format and extreme planetary science niche while exploring a completely fresh astronomical phenomenon not yet covered in our channel history.

experiment: A/B test the classic 'What If' hook against a direct threat hook ('You Would Die in 0.3 Seconds on This Planet') within the space category to determine which drives higher initial 24-hour velocity and retention.
